title: Unsupervised machine learning identifies early stage breast cancer subclasses from aberrant glycogene expression and informs personalised drug treatment.
summary: GHSORM clustering of glycogene expression in 785 early-stage breast-cancer samples identified seven expression subclasses, and RFES selected 60 genes that classified the clusters with 90.48% accuracy on a held-out set. I-SPY2 pCR patterns are retrospective and exploratory; the study does not establish prospective treatment-selection benefit.
ai_technology: GHSORM clustering and random-forest feature selection

evidence.tested: GHSORM clustering of glycogene expression in 785 early-stage breast-cancer samples identified seven expression subclasses, and RFES selected 60 genes that classified the clusters with 90.48% accuracy on a held-out set. I-SPY2 pCR patterns are retrospective and exploratory; the study does not establish prospective treatment-selection benefit.
evidence.unknown: The study evaluates the reported models and datasets only; broader generalization and real-world deployment outcomes were not established.
evidence.ai_role: GHSORM hierarchical self-organizing-map clustering defines glycogene-expression subclasses; random-forest feature selection and classification predicts those subclasses.
